title: Guimaras Royale Cashew: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: Guimaras Royale Cashew: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Guimaras Royale cashew is a cashew variety from Glen Espartero. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Guimaras Royale is a registered cashew variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2019 as NSIC 2019 Cs 09. Glen Espartero bred it. Its record notes a yield of 350 to 400 fruits.

blocks.text: Key facts about Guimaras Royale cashew
When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Guimaras Royale was about 10 years old and about more than 10 meters tall when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 350 to 400 fruits. It bears every year, with fruit in March May. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit cashew fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug), [powdery mildew](/diseases/powdery-mildew), [thrips](/pests/thrips). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its sweetness measured 11.89 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. Its fruiting season is March May, bearing annual.
Where and when to plant Guimaras Royale cashew

Kasoy stands drought and poor soil, which is why Palawan grows so much of it. Pick a selection by nut weight and shelling recovery, which decide the kernel you sell. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
